---
title: "Local ticket NLP with quackformers + duckboost"
---

Support tickets usually mix **free-form text** with a few structured columns. This vignette is an example of pairing **duckboost** with other DuckDB extensions to do that kind of NLP work **entirely inside DuckDB** — local embeddings, SQL labeling, and GBDT training/scoring — **without a separate Python/ML runtime or hosted model API**.

| Step | Extension | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Embed subject + body | Community [`quackformers`](https://duckdb.org/community_extensions/extensions/quackformers.html) | `embed()` ≈ [`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`](https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) (384-d) |
| Optional ANN index | Core [`vss`](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/core_extensions/vss.html) | HNSW over `FLOAT[384]` when the corpus is large |
| Train / score | **duckboost** | Binary or multiclass GBDT on numeric features from those embeddings (+ any other columns) |

duckboost only accepts `DOUBLE[]` features. Text enters the model **through embeddings** (and optional lexical extras), not as raw `VARCHAR`.

The worked example routes tickets between two clearly different queues — **Technical Support** vs **Billing and Payments** — using a public support-ticket corpus. The same pattern extends to more labels once your taxonomy and prototypes are solid.

::: {.callout-note}
## Dataset

Examples use a balanced English sample (400 tickets per queue) from Tobias Bueck's [Customer Support Tickets](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Tobi-Bueck/customer-support-tickets) corpus (also on [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tobiasbueck/email-ticket-text-german-classification)). The Hugging Face mirror is licensed **CC BY-NC 4.0** — non-commercial use with attribution. See [Credits](#credits).
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Docs execution on DuckDB 2.0 alpha

This repository builds against DuckDB 2.0 alpha (`v2.0-cyanoptera`). Community `quackformers` is not published for that pin on the community CDN yet, so the **numbers on this page** use the **same MiniLM-L6-v2 model** offline via a cached Parquet sample. The SQL in the fences is the recipe for a DuckDB build where `INSTALL quackformers FROM community` works (current 1.x community builds). Replace the precomputed `emb` column with `embed(text)::FLOAT[384]` when you run it yourself.
:::

## 1. Load tickets from a public URL

On a released DuckDB with `httpfs` / community autoload:

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
INSTALL quackformers FROM community; LOAD quackformers;

CREATE TABLE tickets AS
SELECT
  row_number() OVER () AS ticket_id,
  subject,
  body,
  queue,
  priority,
  language,
  type,
  concat_ws(E'\n', subject, body) AS text
FROM read_csv(
  'https://huggingface.co/datasets/Tobi-Bueck/customer-support-tickets/resolve/main/aa_dataset-tickets-multi-lang-5-2-50-version.csv'
)
WHERE lower(language) = 'en'
  AND queue IN ('Technical Support', 'Billing and Payments')
  AND subject IS NOT NULL
  AND body IS NOT NULL;
```

```sql
SELECT
  queue,
  count(*) AS n,
  round(avg(len(text)), 0) AS avg_chars
FROM tickets_emb
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
```

```text
┌──────────────────────┬─────┬───────────┐
│        queue         │  n  │ avg_chars │
├──────────────────────┼─────┼───────────┤
│ Billing and Payments │ 400 │ 395.0     │
│ Technical Support    │ 400 │ 400.0     │
└──────────────────────┴─────┴───────────┘
```


## 2. Local embeddings with quackformers

```sql
CREATE TABLE tickets_emb AS
SELECT
  ticket_id, subject, body, queue, priority, language, type, text,
  embed(text)::FLOAT[384] AS emb
FROM tickets;
```

`embed()` returns a 384-d float vector (MiniLM). For a larger in-extension model, quackformers also exposes `embed_jina()` (768-d). Pair with core `vss` if you want an HNSW index over `emb` for nearest-ticket search at larger scale; this page uses direct cosine similarity.

## 3. Deterministic labels from a fixed label set

Keep a small catalog of labels you control. Embed each prototype once with the same model, then assign every ticket the prototype with the highest cosine similarity. Same prototypes + same embedder ⇒ same labels.

```sql
SELECT queue, prototype
FROM label_prototypes
ORDER BY queue;
```

```text
┌──────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│        queue         │                                                             prototype                                                             │
├──────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Billing and Payments │ Invoices, charges, refunds, payment failures, billing disputes, subscriptions, receipts, and account balance questions.           │
│ Technical Support    │ Technical issues with software applications, bugs, crashes, errors, configuration problems, failed features, and troubleshooting. │
└──────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ticket_labels AS
SELECT
  t.ticket_id,
  t.queue AS gold_queue,
  t.priority,
  arg_max(p.queue, array_cosine_similarity(t.emb, p.emb)) AS assigned_queue,
  max(array_cosine_similarity(t.emb, p.emb)) AS best_sim,
  [
    max(array_cosine_similarity(t.emb, p.emb)) FILTER (WHERE p.queue = 'Billing and Payments'),
    max(array_cosine_similarity(t.emb, p.emb)) FILTER (WHERE p.queue = 'Technical Support'),
    len(t.text)::DOUBLE,
    (lower(t.priority) = 'high')::DOUBLE,
    (lower(t.priority) = 'medium')::DOUBLE
  ]::DOUBLE[] AS sim_features,
  (list_transform(t.emb, lambda x: x::DOUBLE))::DOUBLE[] AS emb_features
FROM tickets_emb t
CROSS JOIN label_prototypes p
GROUP BY t.ticket_id, t.queue, t.priority, t.text, t.emb;

SELECT
  round(avg((assigned_queue = gold_queue)::INT), 3) AS prototype_match_rate,
  round(avg(best_sim), 3) AS mean_best_cosine
FROM ticket_labels;
```

```text
┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────┐
│ prototype_match_rate │ mean_best_cosine │
├──────────────────────┼──────────────────┤
│ 0.833                │ 0.326            │
└──────────────────────┴──────────────────┘
```


Prototype matching is a **deterministic baseline / weak labeler**. When agents already set `queue` (as in this corpus), use gold labels for supervised training and keep Stage 3 for unlabeled tickets or low-confidence review (for example a small margin between the top two cosine scores).

## 4. Train duckboost on embedding features

Map the two queues to `{0, 1}`, hold out a stratified test split, and fit a binary native model on the **full 384-d embedding** (plus you can concatenate structured columns). Compact alternative: train only on the prototype cosine scores in `sim_features`.

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ticket_labels AS
SELECT
  t.ticket_id,
  t.queue AS gold_queue,
  (t.queue = 'Technical Support')::DOUBLE AS y,
  (list_transform(t.emb, lambda x: x::DOUBLE))::DOUBLE[] AS features
FROM tickets_emb t;

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ticket_model_rows AS
SELECT l.*, s.split
FROM ticket_labels l
JOIN (
  SELECT ticket_id, split
  FROM duckboost_initial_split('ticket_labels', prop := 0.75, strata := gold_queue, seed := 7)
) s USING (ticket_id);

CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, features,
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'task': 'binary',
    'n_estimators': '80',
    'max_depth': '4',
    'learning_rate': '0.1',
    'colsample_bytree': '0.5',
    'seed': '7'
  }
) AS model
FROM ticket_model_rows
WHERE split = 'train';

SELECT
  round(duckboost_evaluate_agg(model, y, features, MAP {'metric': 'accuracy'}), 3) AS test_accuracy,
  round(duckboost_evaluate_agg(model, y, features, MAP {'metric': 'logloss'}), 3) AS test_logloss
FROM models, ticket_model_rows
WHERE split = 'test';
```

```text
┌───────────────┬──────────────┐
│ test_accuracy │ test_logloss │
├───────────────┼──────────────┤
│ 0.825         │ 0.43         │
└───────────────┴──────────────┘
```


A few scored rows with class probabilities:

```sql
SELECT
  gold_queue,
  round(duckboost_predict(model, features), 0) AS pred_tech,
  round(duckboost_predict_proba(model, features)[2], 3) AS p_technical
FROM models, ticket_model_rows
WHERE split = 'test'
ORDER BY ticket_id
LIMIT 8;
```

```text
┌──────────────────────┬───────────┬─────────────┐
│      gold_queue      │ pred_tech │ p_technical │
├──────────────────────┼───────────┼─────────────┤
│ Billing and Payments │ 0.0       │ 0.001       │
│ Technical Support    │ 1.0       │ 0.987       │
│ Technical Support    │ 1.0       │ 0.913       │
│ Technical Support    │ 1.0       │ 0.973       │
│ Technical Support    │ 0.0       │ 0.249       │
│ Billing and Payments │ 0.0       │ 0.008       │
│ Technical Support    │ 0.0       │ 0.277       │
│ Billing and Payments │ 1.0       │ 0.506       │
└──────────────────────┴───────────┴─────────────┘
```


## 5. Scoring and export

Predict with `duckboost_predict` / `duckboost_predict_proba`, or emit plain SQL with `duckboost_to_sql` for inference sessions that do not load duckboost. Rebuilding features still needs `quackformers` (or a stored `emb` column) wherever you score new tickets.

## Adapting this to your tickets

1. Keep a small `label_prototypes` table for your taxonomy (queues, priority bands, issue types, …).
2. Embed ticket text with [`quackformers`](https://duckdb.org/community_extensions/extensions/quackformers.html) (`embed` or `embed_jina`).
3. Assign weak labels from prototype cosine when gold labels are missing; prefer gold labels when agents already set them.
4. Feed `emb::DOUBLE[]` and any structured columns into `duckboost_train`.
5. Optionally index embeddings with core `vss` for nearest-neighbor triage at larger scale.
6. For many overlapping queues, start with a coarse split (as here) or hierarchical routing before a flat multiclass over dozens of labels.
